nonblocking_findings: NB1 [Minor] score-impact: no. The refusal branches of --pilot-routes have no test. review-score.test.ts F1 (lines 911-996) covers only the two happy paths: the zero-pass row with and without the reason. No test pins the refusal on a missing file, on an unreadable or invalid-JSON file, or on a non-array file, and no test pins that the refusal never echoes the path or a value. I verified each branch by direct probe: missing file, directory, non-array JSON, and non-JSON text each print only 'score: pilot-routes' with exit 2 (review-score.ts:587-600). The refusals work; the gap is test coverage only. Fix: add one R-series refusal case with a temp non-array file.

NB2 [Nit] score-impact: no. The pilot array validation is lenient (review-score.ts:601-604). An item that is not an object with a string route drops silently; a route of empty string skips silently; a duplicate route dedupes silently. A malformed pilot file therefore under-reports routes with no signal. The pinned contract demands refusal only for a missing, unreadable, or non-array file, so this stays within spec. Fix: refuse an array that holds any item without a string route.

NB3 [Nit] score-impact: no. A pilot route string that matches a key shape lands unscanned in two committed files: the pilot file itself and the score file route row. The KEY_SHAPE_RE guard covers --incomplete-reason only (review-score.ts:584-586 vs :601-604). This extends the recorded N1 prevention gap (tech-debt.md, Review B 4b N1) to the new input path. No leak exists at HEAD: the grep over both committed files finds no key shape and leak-check exits 0. Fix: run KEY_SHAPE_RE over each pilot route before the write.
